new_foods.source: PROVISIONAL (nalt-names-14): Martinez Steele et al., J Nutr2023 Table1 Group1, "Natural, packaged, cut, chilled or frozen vegetables, fruits, potatoes, cassava, and other roots and tubers"; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10127522/ . Exact term celery is not named: class-instance of plain vegetables, not an exact-named food or placement supplied by NALT. Plain edible celery vegetable, including the documented stalk/leaf food types, not an alias to celery seed or celeriac. NALT Product11117 identifies celery under vegetables (https://lod.nal.usda.gov/nalt/en/page/11117). UMass separately describes stalk celery, leaf celery and culinary stalk/leaf uses (https://www.umass.edu/agriculture-food-environment/nutrition/publications-resources/produce-spotlight/celery); Illinois Extension independently describes celery leaves as an edible cooking part (https://extension.illinois.edu/blogs/wow-words-wellness-lifestyle-blog/2020-04-10-save-money-using-whole-plant). This is not permission for a seed, juice, extract, celery salt or a recipe. Conditional minimal-process scope from Monteiro et al., FAO2019 Table1 Group1 (https://www.fao.org/4/ca5644en/ca5644en.pdf): "Unprocessed foods altered by industrial processes such as removal of inedible or unwanted parts, drying, powdering, squeezing, crushing, grinding, fractioning, steaming, poaching, boiling, roasting, and pasteurization, chilling, freezing, placing in containers, vacuum packaging, non-alcoholic fermentation, and other methods that do not add salt, sugar, oils or fats or other food substances to the original food." Explicit same-original-food-only composition is required for ambiguous grinding/powder forms; unknown powders, flours, extracts, oils, recipes, unspecified preservation and unrelated plant parts get no plain-food permission. Not a strong marker. Item-own culinary additions are separately supported by Martinez Steele et al. Table1 Group3: "These are relatively simple products manufactured essentially with the addition of salt or sugar or other substances of common culinary use, such as oil or vinegar, to unprocessed or minimally processed foods." Existing guards for salt/sugar/brine and unknown conditions remain item-scoped and unchanged.

aliases.source: Current2026-11-22 naming/physical-food identity only: NALT Product127499 names (https://lod.nal.usda.gov/nalt/en/page/127499) and independent Iowa State/Purdue explicit green-onion/scallion food identity (https://yardandgarden.extension.iastate.edu/how-to/all-about-onions; https://www.extension.purdue.edu/foodlink/food.php?food=onion%2C+green+onion%2C+scallion); no spring-onion maturity equivalence. NALT CC BY4.0. Not NOVA placement or a strong marker; target food, part and item-own form conditions retained (nalt-names-14).

notes: Five overlapping vegetable/edible-part heads and one alias, not disjoint-food counts or a coverage estimate.
Green and spring onions retain independently supported maturity distinctions.
Beet/root additions remain held: current shared descriptor stripping confuses beet red colour with the whole root when100%/whole is present. No guard, marker or importer change.
The older beetroot-powder row and every tested old route are preserved; beet greens has a source-only leafy-vegetable citation correction.
